info.title: ezacto API
info.description: The native ezacto v1 contract. Contract and generated clients are deterministic build artifacts. An operator can switch whole modules off (SSO_ENABLED, BACKUPS_ENABLED, INVOICES_ENABLED, ACCOUNTING_ENABLED, each `true` or `false`): every operation of a switched-off module answers 403 `module_disabled`, makes no provider call and leaves its data untouched.

post.summary: Create or start a time entry
post.description: `started_time` with `ended_time` logs a stopped start/end entry in either organization mode, its `seconds` derived from the two times (an end before the start is past midnight); `seconds` beside them is 422 `mode_mismatch`. Without times the organization's `time_entry_mode` decides: in `duration`, `seconds` logs a stopped entry and leaving it out starts a timer; in `start_end`, leaving out `ended_time` starts a timer at the current local time and `seconds` is 422 `mode_mismatch`. A timer in a `duration` organization never carries times, so `started_time` without `ended_time` there is 422 `mode_mismatch`. Entries may overlap; each counts its own full duration.

get.summary: Get a time entry

patch.description: An entry keeps the shape it was created with, whatever the organization's mode: a start/end entry takes `started_time` and `ended_time` and re-derives `seconds`, a duration entry takes `seconds`, and the other is 422 `mode_mismatch`.

post.summary: Stop a time entry
Restart a time entry

get.summary: List the acting user's calendar events offered as time
get.description: Only the acting user's own, administrators included. A proposal is a calendar event held beside the timesheet, not a time entry: it reaches no report, lock or invoice until it is accepted. `status` defaults to `proposed`, what is waiting for a decision. `from` and `to` are calendar days on the user's own calendar, both included, and filter on the day the event starts.

post.summary: Accept a calendar proposal as a time entry
post.description: Creates the entry through the same path as `POST /time-entries`, so rounding, timesheet locks, approval membership, assignment and note rules all apply, and marks the proposal accepted in the same write. In a `duration` organization the entry carries the event's length and no times; in `start_end` it carries the event's times on the user's own clock, and an event that runs past local midnight is 422 `spans_days`. `notes` defaults to the event's title. The proposal's `time_entry_id` and the `Location` header name the entry. A proposal already decided is 409 `proposal_not_open`, and nothing is created.

post.summary: Discard a calendar proposal
post.description: A discarded event is not offered again when the calendar is read again. A proposal already decided is 409 `proposal_not_open`.

get.summary: List planned allocations
get.description: Planned hours per week for a person on a project over a range of dates. Administrators and executive managers read all of them; a project manager reads their own and those for the people and projects they manage; everyone else reads only their own. `from` and `to` keep the allocations that reach into that span of days. A plan is not work: it is separate from time entries and never billed.

post.summary: Plan hours for a person on a project
post.description: Administrators, executive managers and project managers only, a project manager only for people and projects they manage. Dates are plain local days, both included; the figure counts in full for every week the range touches. An end before the start is 422 `invalid_range`, an archived or unknown person or project is 422 `inactive_user`, `inactive_project`, `unknown_user` or `unknown_project`, and a range that overlaps another for the same person and project is 409 `allocation_overlap`. Planning more than a person's capacity is allowed: the capacity view flags it.

get.summary: Get an allocation

patch.description: Dates and hours only: the person and project of a plan do not change, so to move one, delete it and make another. The same rules as creating apply, and a plan changed by someone else in the meantime is 409 `allocation_changed`.

delete.description: Send the version last read in the JSON body. A stale version is 409; omitted versions are deprecated until the 2027-01-22 sunset, then refused.

get.summary: Read planned hours against capacity and tracked time, person by week
get.description: Read-only. Weeks begin on the organization's week start day and run from the week holding `from` through the week holding `to`, at most 53. Per person and week: `planned_seconds` (the sum of the allocations touching that week, on active projects), `weekly_capacity_seconds` (the person's current weekly capacity, so part-time is honoured), `tracked_seconds` (rounded time actually logged, a separate figure and never changed by the plan) and `over_allocated` when planned exceeds capacity, which is a flag and never a refusal. Archived people are left out. Administrators and executive managers see everyone, a project manager the people they manage, everyone else only themselves.

get.summary: List time off
get.description: Days a person is away, entered by an administrator. Administrators and executive managers read all of it; a project manager reads their own and that of the people they manage; everyone else reads only their own. `from` and `to` keep the entries that reach into that span of days. Time off reduces the capacity the capacity view counts as available; it is not work, is never billed, and has no approval step.

post.summary: Enter time off for a person
post.description: Administrators, executive managers and project managers only, a project manager only for the people they manage. Dates are plain local days, both included; only Monday to Friday remove capacity. `seconds_per_day` null is a whole day (a fifth of the person's weekly capacity); a figure is that many seconds away on each working day. An end before the start or an unknown `kind` is 422, an archived or unknown person is 422 `inactive_user` or `unknown_user`, and a range that overlaps other time off for the same person is 409 `time_off_overlap`, so a day is never taken off twice.

get.summary: Get time off

patch.description: Dates, kind and hours only: the person does not change, so to move time off to someone else, delete it and make another. The same rules as creating apply, and an entry changed by someone else in the meantime is 409 `time_off_changed`.

delete.description: Send the version last read in the JSON body. A stale version is 409; omitted versions are deprecated until the 2027-01-22 sunset, then refused.

List invoices
get.description: Newest first: by issue_date, latest first; then by number, highest first -- compared as a number when it is made of digits alone (leading zeros ignored) and as text, by Unicode code point, otherwise, with all-digit numbers ahead of the rest on a day that has both; then by id, highest first, so no two invoices tie. The first page fixes the traversal to the invoices that existed when it was read: an invoice created after it does not appear on later pages of the same traversal, and is listed by a new one. Editing an invoice's issue_date or number moves it in the order, so a traversal already under way may miss it or list it twice. The number parameter narrows the list to the invoice with exactly that number, compared as text, so 089 is not 89; numbers are unique, so the page holds that invoice or nothing. The sort parameter orders by issue_date, due_date, number, amount or balance, with - in front for descending (the default is -issue_date, the order above). The chosen column ranks first, then the number, then the id, all in the one direction. A cursor belongs to the sort it was issued under and is refused under another.

Get the rate card attached to a client
get.description: The card attached directly to this client, with every version, oldest first; inheritance is not applied (use the effective lookup for that). 404 `rate_card_not_found` when the client has no card. Billable rates are money: only the profiles that may see billable rates (administrator, accounting, executive manager, and a project manager granted `billable_rates_manager`) read a card, and everyone else is 403 `money_forbidden`.

post.summary: Attach a named rate card to a client
post.description: A client has at most one card (409 `rate_card_exists`); change its rates by adding a version. The card starts with no versions and prices nothing until one is added. Same visibility rule as reading, and the caller must also be allowed to write clients.

post.summary: Append a version to a client's rate card
post.description: Versions are append-only and effective-dated: the version in force on a date is the one with the latest `start_date` on or before it, and a null `start_date` means all prior dates. A new version must start after every existing one (409 `rate_card_version_order`); a correction is simply a later version. A line with a null `task_id` is the card default; a task line wins for that task. An empty `lines` array retires the card, so it is skipped and the next ancestor's card applies. Adding a version prices work resolved afterwards; it never changes an existing entry, snapshot or invoice, and existing entries change only through the audited reprice.

get.summary: Look up the card rate that prices a task for a client
get.description: Walks the client and its ancestors through `parent_client_id` only (never the bill-to client), nearest first, with the same rules the rate resolver uses: a card with no version in force, an empty version, or no line for the task and no default line is skipped. `supplied_by_client_id` is the node whose card priced it and `depth` how far up that node sits (0 is the client itself). The card prices only projects billed by people that use default rates. `spent_date` defaults to today in the instance time zone. 404 `rate_card_not_found` when no card prices it.

post.summary: Reauthenticate an administrator for temporary draft invoice edits
post.description: Requires an administrator API token with invoices:write, live password authentication, and the same verified user credentials. Confirmed authenticator or email MFA requires a bound second step. The returned capability belongs to this base token and invoice, lasts at most 15 minutes, and is returned once. Credential responses cannot be replayed from the HTTP cache.

post.summary: Complete the bound second factor for a draft invoice elevation
post.description: A valid MFA challenge can only be completed by its original administrator and base API token. The verified capability never creates a browser session.

post.description: Administrator API token only; requires invoices:write, time_entries:write and X-Ezacto-Invoice-Elevation bound to this invoice. All selected stopped entries must still belong to the same current draft. The whole command and its before/after audit commit together. Invoice line amounts remain unchanged.

InsufficientPermissionOrModuleDisabled.description: Insufficient permission, or `module_disabled`: the operator of this instance switched the module off

signing_secret.description: Copy once. Store securely at the receiver; never logged or returned by list endpoints.

password.description: At most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; never an argv argument or a stored CLI setting.

credential.description: Returned once; keep only in process memory and send as X-Ezacto-Invoice-Elevation with the original API token.

cadence.description: Monthly M H D * * on the organization clock; skipped calendar days do not run.
Monthly M H D * * on the organization clock; skipped calendar days do not run.

ActivityLogActor.description: Who caused the event. type and id are what the event recorded; name is resolved when the log is read, so it is the person's current name. name is null for a system actor and for an id that no user or contact carries any more.

GeneralResource.description: Commercial fields are omitted without finance/admin authority or an explicit billable_rates_manager grant. The same authority is required to set them; resource read/write scopes still apply.

GeneralMutationInput.description: Commercial fields listed on GeneralResource require the same commercial authority for create and update, in addition to resource write scope.

expires_at.description: Omitted: the token expires one year after issue. Anyone may ask for a sooner expiry; only an administrator may ask for one more than a year away or for null (never). Others are refused with 422 and code too_long.

invoice_id.description: Omitted without invoices:read authority (profile and token).

is_billed.description: Omitted without invoices:read authority (profile and token).

user_id.description: Whose entry. Defaults to the acting user. Only an administrator may name somebody else, and only for stopped time: a timer is started by the person it tracks.

seconds.description: A duration entry's length. Not accepted with started_time or ended_time.

started_time.description: Canonical 24-hour HH:MM. With ended_time, a stopped start/end entry in either organization mode.

ended_time.description: Canonical 24-hour HH:MM. Requires started_time and spent_date.

occurrence.description: Tells the instances of a recurring event apart; empty otherwise.

time_entry_id.description: The entry an accepted proposal became; null until then.

planned_seconds_per_week.description: Planned seconds in each week the range touches, between 1 and 604800.

version.description: Version last read. Required from 2027-01-22; supplied values are always enforced.

time_off_seconds.description: Capacity removed by the person's time off in the week (Monday to Friday only, never more than the capacity).

available_capacity_seconds.description: `weekly_capacity_seconds` less `time_off_seconds`; what the plan is held against.

tracked_seconds.description: Rounded time logged in the week; separate from the plan.

over_allocated.description: Planned exceeds available capacity (capacity less time off). A flag for the reader, never a refusal.

seconds_per_day.description: Seconds away on each working day, between 1 and 86400; null is a whole day.

version.description: Version last read. Required from 2027-01-22; supplied values are always enforced.

credential_configured.description: Whether the deployment holds the provider's credential. The credential is never returned.

item_id.description: The provider's own identity for the item.

EffectiveTimeRounding.description: The rule an entry on a project is saved under, and whose it is.

invoice_id.description: Omitted without invoices:read authority (profile and token).

is_billed.description: Omitted without invoices:read authority (profile and token).

report.description: The Reports kind, such as time or invoiced.

query.description: The report's query string: filters, grouping, sort and range.

task_id.description: The task this rate is for; null is the card default.

start_date.description: First day this version is in force; null means all prior dates.

task_id.description: The matching line's task; null when the card default priced it.
